title: Infrastructure: offline audio stack (STT / TTS / wake word) + supplemental files
purpose: Offline audio engine for the robot/kiosk stack: Speech-to-Text with faster-whisper (CTranslate2, local_files_only=True), Text-to-Speech with Piper ONNX neural voices falling back to the system pyttsx3 engine, and a low-power background wake-word detector ('Hey Campus' / 'Hey Sparky'). This subsystem was missed by the initial scan and is documented here as a supplement. It is an alternative/parallel offline implementation to the older services/stt_service.py, services/tts_service.py and services/vad_service.py; the audio package is the canonical offline one referenced by the infrastructure package.

files.purpose: Package marker for the infrastructure package (adapters for external services and local storage).
Public exports for the audio package: STTService, FasterWhisperSTTService, TTSService, NonBlockingTTSService.
files.notes: Re-exports the protocols and the offline implementations.

files.purpose: Offline Speech-to-Text: STTService protocol, STTResult (str subclass with language/confidence metadata), and FasterWhisperSTTService backed by faster-whisper's CTranslate2 engine.

terms.definition: Speech-to-Text: converts spoken audio to transcribed text.
CTranslate2-accelerated reimplementation of OpenAI Whisper, run locally (local_files_only=True).
Voice Activity Detection filter (vad_filter=True) that skips non-speech segments before transcription.
Whisper decoding beam width; 1 = greedy decoding for low latency.
Whisper's estimated probability the audio contains no speech; > 0.6 is treated as silence and skipped.
Root-mean-square signal level used to reject silent/too-quiet audio before transcription.
SpeechRecognition energy cutoff for detecting speech onset; recalibrated for ambient noise on start.

files.notes: Offline-first: local_files_only=True, compute type forced to int8 on CPU. Microphone auto-selection filters virtual/loopback devices (fxsound, mapper, stereo mix, virtual, steam) and prefers Realtek/microphone-array devices. An optional Google Speech API fallback exists but is gated behind enable_online_fallback=False. Streaming mode transcribes a sliding 250ms window with an initial_prompt of campus vocabulary and filters hallucinated prompt text.

files.purpose: Offline Text-to-Speech: TTSService protocol and NonBlockingTTSService using Piper ONNX neural voices (en/English, hi/Hindi) with a pyttsx3 system-engine fallback (used for Kannada, which has no Piper voice) and a background worker-thread speech queue.

terms.definition: Text-to-Speech: synthesizes spoken audio from text.
Local neural TTS engine using ONNX voice models (e.g. en_US-lessac-medium).
Cross-platform system TTS engine used as a fallback when no Piper voice exists (e.g. Kannada).
TTS returns immediately and plays audio on a background worker thread so the UI never stalls.
Cancelling queued/playing TTS instantly so a user can interrupt the robot mid-speech.
speak_stream splits an LLM token generator into sentences and enqueues them for near-real-time speech.

files.notes: Multilingual: English/Hindi use Piper; Kannada and missing-model cases fall back to pyttsx3; if neither engine is available it only logs (simulated speech). cancel_playback flushes the queue and stops the PyAudio stream for barge-in.

files.purpose: Low-power background wake-word detector ('Hey Campus' / 'Hey Sparky'): a daemon thread reads 80ms frames from a sounddevice InputStream and triggers a callback on detection.

terms.definition: A phrase that activates the robot from a low-power listening state (e.g. 'Hey Campus').
Optional library providing ONNX wake-word models (here 'hey_jarvis_v0.1'); gracefully skipped if not installed.
Fallback heuristic that triggers on a speech-onset spike (energy > 0.18, peak > 0.45, zero-crossing count 10-300).
How often the waveform crosses zero, used to distinguish vocal energy from white noise.
A 2-second lockout after a trigger to prevent double-firing.

files.notes: OpenWakeWord is optional; the acoustic burst classifier is a heuristic stand-in when the model is absent. Stream errors fall back to event-driven audio mode.

files.purpose: Unit test verifying OllamaLLMService sends the configured model, a single user-role message, generation options and stream=False to the Ollama client, and that the reply is whitespace-stripped.
files.notes: Uses a FakeOllamaClient capturing the chat call without connecting to Ollama; confirms a single 'user' role message (no separate system role).

files.purpose: The generator script that produces Campus_Helpdesk_Complete_Architecture.docx from the .architecture_scan/ reports; a documentation tool, not part of the runtime system.
files.notes: Uses python-docx. Consumes the JSON reports emitted by the architecture-scan workflow.

data_flow: Infrastructure audio is consumed by the robot stack: the wake-word detector runs continuously; once triggered, STT records and transcribes user speech (faster-whisper, offline), the transcript is answered by the RAG pipeline, and the answer is spoken by TTS (Piper/pyttsx3). STT can also wait on TTS playback to finish before opening the microphone. The package is exported through infrastructure/__init__.py for the rest of src/campus_helpdesk.
risks: Duplication: infrastructure/audio/* is a parallel offline implementation of services/stt_service.py, services/tts_service.py and services/vad_service.py; both exist and can drift.
STT Google fallback is an online service gated by a flag; enabling it breaks the offline-first guarantee.
Wake-word fallback classifier is heuristic (energy/peak/zero-crossings) and not a true model; openwakeword's 'hey_jarvis' model does not match the configured phrase.
TTS silently degrades to simulated speech (log only) if both Piper and pyttsx3 are unavailable.
